description: Practical cognitive-bias lens packs organised by real decisions rather than by bias name.

packs.title: Career Decision Lens Pack
packs.summary: A practical review for job changes, promotions, offers and long-term career choices.
useWhen: deciding whether to leave a role
choosing a new skill or career direction

lenses.name: Anchoring effect
lenses.question: What would I think this offer was worth if I had not seen the first number?

lenses.name: Sunk cost / escalation of commitment
lenses.question: If I had not already invested years here, would I still choose the next year?

lenses.name: Projection bias
lenses.question: Am I treating my current mood as a forecast of my future preferences?

lenses.name: Planning fallacy
lenses.question: What happened to people who made a similar transition, not just in my ideal plan?

lenses.name: Outcome bias
lenses.question: Am I copying someone's career because it worked, without checking the process and luck?

workflow: Write the decision and the date by which you need to decide.
Set three criteria before comparing options.
Create your own estimate before asking a recruiter, manager or AI for one.
Write one strong reason against your preferred option.
Review the choice from the perspective of your future self six months later.

packs.title: AI-Assisted Work Lens Pack
packs.summary: A review for using AI without quietly outsourcing judgment, evidence checks or memory.
useWhen: using an agent to make repeated decisions

lenses.name: Automation bias
lenses.question: Would I accept this answer if it came from an unknown junior colleague?

lenses.name: Anchoring effect
lenses.question: Did the model's first answer become the centre of my later reasoning?

lenses.name: Anthropomorphism
lenses.question: Am I reacting to fluent humanlike language instead of tested capability?

lenses.name: Source confusion
lenses.question: Can I still tell which claims came from me, the source material and the model?

lenses.name: Confirmation bias
lenses.question: Did I ask AI to test my view or mainly to make it sound stronger?

workflow: Form a first view before asking AI when the decision is important.
Ask for assumptions, missing evidence and the strongest alternative explanation.
Keep source links next to important claims.
Separate generated text from verified facts.
Record the final human decision and why it differs from the model, if it does.

packs.title: Team Decision Lens Pack
packs.summary: A practical meeting and review workflow for reducing agreement pressure and hidden assumptions.

lenses.name: Bandwagon effect
lenses.question: Would people make the same choice if they voted before hearing the room?

lenses.name: Authority bias
lenses.question: Are we evaluating the argument or the seniority of the person saying it?

lenses.name: Confirmation bias
lenses.question: Which evidence would make the team stop or change direction?

lenses.name: Outcome bias
lenses.question: Are we reviewing the quality of the decision process, not only the result?

lenses.name: Hindsight bias
lenses.question: What did we actually predict before the outcome was known?

workflow: Collect independent views before open discussion.
Write the decision criteria where everyone can see them.
Assign one person to present the strongest case against the current favourite.
Record uncertainty and what would change the decision.
Review the original reasoning after the outcome, not a reconstructed memory of it.

packs.title: Product & Project Decision Lens Pack
packs.summary: A compact review for estimates, pivots, roadmaps, launches and stopping rules.

lenses.name: Planning fallacy
lenses.question: What is the outside-view duration from comparable completed work?

lenses.name: Escalation of commitment
lenses.question: Would we fund the next step if the project arrived today with no history?

lenses.name: Pro-innovation bias
lenses.question: Which costs, failure modes or adoption barriers are missing from the exciting story?

lenses.name: Survivorship bias
lenses.question: Which failed projects are absent from the examples we are copying?

lenses.name: Outcome bias
lenses.question: Did this work because the process was good, or because uncertainty happened to favour us?

workflow: Start with a reference class before detailed estimation.
Define a measurable success condition and a stopping condition.
List one adoption risk, one operational risk and one evidence gap.
Run a small reversible test before a large commitment where possible.
After the result, review the original assumptions before changing the playbook.

packs.title: News & Information Lens Pack
packs.summary: A practical check for claims, feeds, repeated stories and AI-generated summaries.

lenses.name: Availability bias
lenses.question: Is this common, or simply vivid and easy to remember?

lenses.name: Illusory truth effect
lenses.question: Have I verified this claim, or just seen it many times?

lenses.name: Common source bias
lenses.question: How many independent sources are there behind these repeated versions?

lenses.name: Confirmation bias
lenses.question: What is the strongest evidence against the explanation I prefer?

lenses.name: Source confusion
lenses.question: Can I trace the important claim back to where it actually came from?

workflow: Separate the claim from the headline or commentary around it.
Find the earliest available primary or direct source.
Count independent evidence, not repeated mentions.
Check the denominator, base rate or comparison class when numbers are involved.
Save the source with the claim if you expect to reuse it later.
